articles.title: Experience: I fell 12 metres while bouldering and smashed my pelvis into pieces
articles.summary: It was clear it was broken. I could feel the bones grinding together as the paramedics strapped me to a gurney. Growing up in Utah, I was so active that my parents nicknamed me “The Blur”. My older siblings introduced me to rock climbing while I was still at primary school.
body: One summer’s day in 2014, when I was 17, my friends and I went paddleboarding on a lake. My friend Trevor and I decided to climb one of the rocky boulders overlooking the water, and jump in.

The rock was about 12 metres tall. I had climbed and jumped from higher. What we hadn’t counted on was a layer of moss that made the boulder slippery. Neither of us had our grippy climbing shoes with us. When I nearly fell, I thought about turning back, but I convinced myself that it was safer to keep going.

From the top, we discovered the water didn’t come right up to the boulder. Instead, there was a swathe of black volcanic rock we would have to clear first. I watched as Trevor took a run-up and hurled himself over the edge. The splash told me he’d safely made it down and into the water.

Normally I’d be excited, but the earlier slip had rattled me. Jumping still felt safer than climbing down, though. I backed up and started to run. As I reached the edge, I hesitated. It was the tiniest pause, but enough to slow my momentum. Instead of leaping outwards, I twisted sideways and started plummeting straight down.
points: I could feel the bones grinding together as the paramedics strapped me to a gurney.

articles.title: The Ninja Slushi Twist is like having a boozy 7-Eleven in your home
articles.summary: The Slushi Twist makes it easy to achieve fantastic, bar-quality drinks without much fuss. The best nonalcoholic wines and nonalcoholic beers in the US. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: Sipping a frozen drink feels like the very essence of a good time. Whether it’s a thick milkshake or a frozen margarita, few people turn down a cold, velvety beverage thick enough to support a straw upright. The appeal seems simple – toss ingredients into a blender, press a button, and enjoy.

But blending drinks in batches can keep a host stuck in the kitchen for hours; why can’t we have a perpetual corkscrew of frozen goodness like a 7-Eleven Slurpee machine? The original Ninja Slushi went viral for delivering precisely this when it arrived in 2024, but it had two key limitations: it could only spin 72oz at a time, and freeze drinks up to 16% alcohol. The new Slushi Twist promises to summon police to your summer barbecues with capacity up to 144oz, stiffer drinks up to 20% alcohol, and mixing them together in a soft-serve-inspired swirl.

As we found out when we tried it, replicating those picture-perfect marketing renderings proved nearly impossible. Skip the Twist if you want Instagram-worthy visuals, but grab it for what it does well: blending fantastic, bar-quality drinks without much fuss.
points: The Slushi Twist makes it easy to achieve fantastic, bar-quality drinks without much fuss.

articles.title: Fat people cannot win, regardless of what we do. And I’ve had enough | Rebecca Shaw
articles.summary: Using weight loss drugs like Ozempic is not ‘cheating’ – and why does it matter how a person changes their body anyway? As you might know if you read my columns, see me a mile away, or talk to me for five seconds, I am a card-carrying lifelong member of the Fat Lesbian Club.
body: It’s not Goodman’s 74-year-old body (his choice) I want to discuss, but instead the arguments that broke out about how he lost the weight. On one side there were many people congratulating him on his hard work. Then there were people claiming he had taken Ozempic so it wasn’t actually hard work, and then there were people defending that by saying he’d been losing weight for years, so he’d done it the “right way”, actually.

I don’t know the details and I don’t care, but none of this is good. This is a common sentiment, but now it seems to be snowballing. There’s this idea that fat people who use weight loss drugs are “cheating” or “taking the easy way”. What it means, as usual, is that fat people cannot win, regardless of what we do. And I’ve had enough.

articles.title: This Underrated California Wine Country Will Transport You Straight to Europe
articles.summary: Want the feel of an Italian or Spanish vineyard vacation, without actually traveling across the Atlantic? Head to Temecula Valley Wine Country.
body: I cheekily open one eye to peer around during shavasana as I lay on my yoga mat between the vines’ full summer foliage at Akash Winery. I’m in Southern California, but the cypress trees and stucco homes suggest an amalgamation of a Tuscan-Provencal hilltop town. I return to darkness for my final deep breaths, grateful for the movement, before another day of wine tasting—which would begin less than five minutes after rolling up my mat and strolling to the tasting room for a breakfast sip of sparkling Sauvignon Blanc.

“Most areas have a signature varietal, but I don’t think we need to pigeonhole ourselves into a certain one,” says Justin Knight, winemaker at Danza Del Sol Winery, as we sip through a delicate yet fruity Albariño, native to Spain’s northwestern Rías Baixas region before switching gears to southern France for a subtly floral Viognier with a delightfully mineral finish.

articles.title: This Jewelry-Designer Bride Created All Her Own Looks for Her Tuscan Castle Wedding
articles.summary: Rene Barnes created six looks using deadstock fabric from Dior, Armani, and Oscar de la Renta to marry Christian DiCroce at a 13th-century castle outside Siena.
body: The pair decided to tie the knot exactly one year later on May 8, 2026, at Castello di Celsa in Italy. Says the bride, “The first time we drove through the gates, I just looked at him, and we both knew this was where we wanted to get married.” Adds the groom, “It just felt like us.” The couple brought an intimate group of friends and family to witness them exchange vows. “We wanted the weekend to feel like an experience rather than just a wedding, so we planned a few days for everyone to slow down and celebrate together,” says Rene.

Naturally, the designer also created all her jewelry for the weekend. “Every piece was designed and made specifically for the look it accompanied, using old European diamonds throughout the collection,” she shares. “I also created our matching wedding bands and a custom diamond brooch for Christian.”

articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. When Google announced the Pixel 11 series last week, it showed off a new "upgrade" for its Pro devices—including the Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and Pixel 11 Pro Fold.
body: Unfortunately, there's nothing else HiLight can do out of the box, which seems like a big missed opportunity for a brand-new hardware feature. Google wants customers to spend more for a Pro device, only to give them two things to do with this Pixel 11 Pro exclusive. And while there's certainly some utility in assigning contacts different colors, to silently know who's calling without needing to pick up your Pixel, there are so many other possibilities for HiLight that the current iteration feels way underbaked.

Enter: HiLight Studio, a new app from developer DhananjayBhosale. DhanajayBhosale's announcement appeared on my X feed, and it immediately caught my attention. The developer designed the app to take full advantage of Google's new hardware, even if Google isn't taking advantage itself. With HiLight Studio, you can assign colors and effects for notifications from any app on your Pixel, not just contacts. Chrome alerts can be blue, WhatsApp alerts can be green, and so on. In addition, you can effectively choose any shade of any color that Android allows, down to saturation and intensity levels.

articles.title: What Garmin's 'Recovery Time' Estimate Actually Means
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. Garmin's fitness watches often give you a "recovery time" after a workout. For example, after one easy run, it told me that I need 21 hours before I'll fully recover.
body: You’ll see your recovery time in the end-of-workout summary that you get right after you finish a workout on many Garmin watches. It’s also available from the Training Status glance on your watch, or the Training Readiness tile in the Garmin Connect app if you have that. On my Forerunner 570, I can even set it as one of the little complications on my main watch face. The recovery time feature is available on most Enduro, Epix, Fenix, Forerunner, Instinct, Venu, and Vivoactive watches, among others (Garmin has a full list here ).

Garmin defines recovery time as “an estimate on how long it will take for you to fully recover and be ready for your next workout of the same intensity.” Note that phrase, fully recover. No athlete is fully recovered at the start of every training session; it's normal to carry a little fatigue from one session to the next. This number is just giving you a sense of how long you’ll be feeling the effects of this workout.
points: Garmin's fitness watches often give you a "recovery time" after a workout.

articles.title: 30+ Best Trench Coats for Women in 2026
articles.summary: Shop Vogue’s guide to the best trench coats for women in 2026, from tried-and-true classics to reimagined silhouettes from Khaite, Burberry, Nour Hammour and more.
body: A classic, beige trench coat is a wardrobe staple that will never go out of style. Thanks to its timeless shape and neutral color palette, the best trench coats for women can do no wrong. They are hardworking outerwear pieces that can transition through the seasons with ease, working for a variety of climates and weather changes (impromptu rain showers, for one!). With summer in its final stretch, we’re looking to fresh fall staples to fill out our wardrobe—starting with the trench coat.

The trench is a coat that has been relied on for decades. In 1879, Thomas Burberry invented gabardine, the weather-proofed, cotton textile the coats were infamously constructed from, making fashion history. Technically, he was outfitting the military, not the style-set at the time, but over the years, the coats have become a stylish staple, featured in many Hollywood films —such as Audrey Hepburn in Breakfast at Tiffany’s to Meryl Streep in Kramer vs. Kramer —and pop culture moments, eventually making the trench coat a bonafide fashion item.

articles.title: In Northern Philippines, Tattoo Artists Attract Travelers in Search of the Most Original Keepsake
articles.summary: Writer Marisol Delarosa makes a pilgrimage to Buscalan, home to 109-year-old Apo Whang-od, the oldest living artist in the country, to meet with the next generation of mambabatoks—and to receive a traditional hand-tapped tattoo of her own.
body: I'm sitting on the balcony of my homestay in Buscalan, a remote mountain village in northern Philippines, reviewing a sheet of tribal tattoo designs with English descriptions: intersecting arrows around layered squares (to represent a compass), zigzagging rows of blackened triangles (mountains), a chain of triangular hourglasses (day and night). Below me a narrow path winds through muddy rice paddies like a snake and disappears into a horizon blanketed by dense fog. January is the middle of the dry season, but the clouds insist otherwise; raindrops are plunking out a tune on the corrugated metal roof.

I decide on a circle orbited by dots and waves: the sun. Maybe this tattoo will usher in the light. This is my third trip to the Philippines, the country my parents left five decades ago. Reaching Buscalan was challenging, starting with a stomach-churning 12-hour drive from Manila through the Cordillera mountains, then a one-hour hike into a ravine of fragrant laurel trees, and finally a rickety tram—a narrow wood crate with a pulley system powered by a stationary Jeep, originally meant for transporting supplies. Still, none of this deters the most resolute.
